strengths: The user's tone example is quoted verbatim as the standard, backed by a typed template: first word 'Phone:' or 'PC only:', expiry in KST, and a line saying what alone is waiting (N.1, N.4).
The separate bot was decided from a live check: the DGIST bot is long-polled and a second poller gets 409, so that bot is only ever used to send (README, N.9).
The phone was checked against the tailnet, and the secret drop (a sealed box through the private repository) keeps long-lived secrets out of Telegram's stored chat history (N.6).

Bridge security is concrete and testable: private chat, matching chat.id and from.id, no forwards, < 24 h age, silent drops, nonce'd buttons, inbound and outbound scrubbing, and crash-safe offsets that account for Telegram's 24 h retention and random update ids (N.5, N.11).

The corrections to SMAT's numbers (symmetry r, the RMSE comparator, the reward confound) are explained to the user with page references. The programme adds the controls the papers lack (B0, A4) and positive controls before any negative verdict (G.1, B.6, README).

The reward algebra (a velocity-proportional optimum, a 27 ms filter, bang-bang in Stage 3) becomes matched baselines B1-B4, and the gate says which numbers test faithfulness and which test mechanism (G.1).

The results are protected from the user too: post-hoc seeds never decide a gate; bands can be corrected only before a claim has results; checkpoints are never chosen by the reported metric; ladder words are enforced by the card validator (G.4, G.8, H.5, C.12).

A measured throughput probe (about 58k transitions/s on CPU and 235k/s on the GPU, 153 MB per process from .mjb, the MULTICCD flag) turns 'hundreds of pipelines' into hours per pipeline and sizes the campaign in days (B.5, RD §4).

Lane isolation is layered (bwrap jail, read-only files, hash checks at start, out-of-band detection, resource fences) and tested by a stateful fuzzer and a scripted rehearsal of every guide action while a job runs (H.4, H.11).
The guide is tested, not trusted: every bash block runs against a throwaway instance, and every PowerShell block is linted for 5.1 (H.10).
The move semantics are the user's own words, kept in bold, with invariants I1-I10, fake back ends, model-based tests, and one real rehearsal capped at USD 5 with a dead-man switch (D.2, E.2).
The forge is protected in detail: distinct names, a disk floor above the forge's, and the gh keyring pitfall caught (GH_CONFIG_DIR plus --insecure-storage) (A.4, N.7).
Plain-language surfaces throughout: six-field cards with 'How sure we are', a validated first-screen summary, and fixed texts for stale or offline states (C.12, D.4).
The README is candid about what was and was not verified, and asks the right open questions (builder mode, author contact, Drive quota, freeing the old project's disk).
The E.6 anti-patterns mirror the user's list almost word for word and add the forge's operational lessons.
